files_changed_self_report.rationale: Completed 021E propose() hardening: new request/response schema, anti-spam enforcement, banner injection, envelope metadata, stdio caller-id derivation, and branch/path response fields.
Updated existing propose stub tests to the hardened API and new `proposals/PROP-NNN` branch shape while preserving prior branch/file behavior checks.
Added acceptance-focused coverage for rate limiting, markdown-normalised dedupe, banner front matter, and proposal envelope fields.
Closed U-21-f with the documented stdio caller-id derivation (`stdio:<pid>:<resolved argv[0] path>`).
Expanded SCP-MCP-E020 text to cover both anti-spam failure modes and their remediation.

self_reported_concerns: The worktree already contained unrelated dispatch-artifact changes under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/021e/`; I left those untouched.

The checked-in repo keyring at `docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub` is still a placeholder in this workspace, so default runtime envelopes fall back to `unconfigured-signing-key` unless the operator-populated keyring is present. The tests cover the configured keyring path explicitly.
codex_structured_result.summary: Implemented WP-SCP-022 Track 2 slice 021E hardening for `propose()`: expanded the MCP request/response schema to include `affected_repos`, `rule_id`, `branch`, `path`, and `pr_url_if_pushed`; added rate limiting (10 proposals per caller per rolling hour), 24-hour body dedupe using markdown-stripped normalised SHA-256 hashes with 1024-hash LRU semantics reconstructed from proposal files, exact silent-rot front-matter/banner injection, and proposal envelope metadata (`mcp_origin`, stdio-derived `caller_id`, `signing_key_id`). I also updated the in-scope error catalogue and closed WP-SCP-021 U-21-f in the plan, refreshed the existing propose tests for the new API/branch naming, added dedicated hardening coverage, and verified the full `tests/scp_mcp` suite passes.
